title: Edge router coalesce + graceful-abort protection for hosted request storms
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
During a high-priority customer escalation we observed correlated 5xx waves originating at the edge router layer when many clients retried in tight intervals. Root cause analysis indicates three compounding issues: (1) upstream request retransmission loops due to absent hop-local idempotency, (2) edge-layer request coalescing behavior triggering large in-flight batches that exceed downstream timeouts, and (3) client-side aborts (connection resets) causing backend tasks to continue and surface 5xx responses to new retrying requests.

Impact observed:
- Multi-tenant latency spikes and ~3% error-rate increase for affected tenants during the incident window.
- Several enterprise customers filed escalations due to failed synchronous calls from web proxies.

Proposed fix (high level):
1) Edge request fingerprinting: compute a lightweight deterministic fingerprint for idempotency (method+path+body-hash+auth-tenant) and attach as X-RW-Req-Fingerprint header at the first edge ingress.
2) In-flight dedup table in edge router: maintain a bounded LRU of recent fingerprints -> promise/future. If a fingerprint is in-flight, new identical requests subscribe to the existing response rather than issuing duplicate upstream calls. This reduces retransmission storms.
3) Graceful-abort propagation: when the client TCP connection closes, edge will send a best-effort cancel to the in-flight promise and mark the subscriber as aborted, but will not cancel the upstream call immediately unless all subscribers have aborted or a configured idle threshold is reached. This prevents brief client retries from causing upstream cancel/retry loops.
4) Downstream timeout hedging and batch-size caps: limit coalesced batch size to N (configurable) and add soft hedging that sends a single early-hedge to a cold replica if latency exceeds the P95 threshold for a given model route.
5) SDK/Proxy guidance: advisable default retry windows increased from 250ms to 600ms and include idempotency fingerprint propagation for SDKs so retries are safe across hops.

Trade-offs considered:
- Latency vs cost: coalescing saves cost and reduces load, but over-coalescing can create head-of-line stalls. We choose conservative defaults (max_coalesce_size=5, max_coalesce_delay=30ms) and expose them per-tenant.
- Memory at edge: in-flight table increases memory usage; bounded LRU with small entries and TTL mitigates risk.
- Correctness vs compatibility: fingerprint composition must be stable across SDK versions; we'll support opt-in for older clients and roll out default enablement after 2-week ramp.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (hotfix config & observability) - 48h: add basic telemetry (fingerprint hit/miss, coalesced_count, subscriber_abort_rate) and a runtime toggle to enable in-flight dedup without turning on cancel semantics. (Owners: Marcus Li, SRE oncall)
- Phase 2 (edge router code) - 1 week: implement dedup table, subscribe/publish promise model, and conservative coalesce caps. Add unit and integration tests in edge-router suite. (Owners: Marcus, Jin Park)
- Phase 3 (graceful-abort + hedging) - 2 weeks: implement abort propagation policy, hedging logic, SDK updates, and e2e load tests. Gradual canary rollout to a low-traffic region. (Owners: Marcus, SDK eng, Observability)
- Phase 4 (rollback & long-term) - Monitor for 2 weeks, adjust defaults, complete stable rollout, and document in runbook. Long-term: consider tenant-aware adaptive coalescing based on historical P95.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and LRU eviction.
- Integration test simulating 10k RPS with retry storms to validate reduction in upstream duplicate calls.
- Canary rollout: start with non-production tenants -> 5 low-volume prod tenants -> broad enablement.
- Monitoring dashboards: new panels for fingerprint_hit_rate, coalesce_avg_size, subscriber_abort_ratio, and upstream_duplicate_calls. Alerting: fire when fingerprint_hit_rate>10% AND upstream_duplicate_calls reduction < 30% after enablement window.

Communication plan:
- Customer-facing: template for support to explain behavior, timing, and compensating controls. Account teams notified with proposed ETA and rollback options.
- Internal: SRE and Oncall rotation to be briefed; Deploy channel and #hosted-api-incidents will be used.

Links and artifacts:
- Postmortem (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HOST/ENG-649201+postmortem
- Load test repo and scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-load-tests/pull/82
- Prototype PR (edge): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/241
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/edge-coalesce-overview

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Default enablement date: target 2026-03-22 if Phase 1 metrics look stable.
- Collision handling policy: current plan is to treat collisions as independent requests (no merge) and log for analysis; prefer to avoid silent incorrect merges.

Acceptance criteria:
- 50% reduction in duplicate upstream calls during synthetic retry storms in canary.
- No increase in P95 latency beyond 8% for coalesced routes.
- No new tenant-visible 5xx regressions in the 72h post-rollout window.
